notes: Cause board for the baselined 8.6%, built at the 2026-07-28 huddle -- the corrected version of the consensus draft the engine refused that morning (fishbone-flawed.json; the refusal and the why are in teaching-note.md). Statuses now carry their evidence: the two vital-few causes hold the pointers the huddle already had -- trim misalignment's mechanism (unsigned imposition) carries the check sheet whose 139 transcribed marks put 67 (48.2%) on trim, wrong paper's mechanism (unlabeled tray loads) carries the tally export the engine Pareto ranked (50 marks, cumulative 84.2% -- the verified vital few) -- and the verification work the draft's statuses were only claiming got done the same day: the prepress walk and the traveler audit behind the 5-Why chain that runs proof-approval -> imposition-from-memory -> unwritten pre-flight, the Improve-ready root the 2026-08-01 rollout memo's checklist targets (with labeled trays as its materials half). Ink cure and lift-counting stay honest candidates in the Pareto's tail (13 and 9 marks); the shift question is ruled out by the chi-square screen (hypothesis-shift, p 0.895 -- the mix is process-shaped, not people-shaped) and rater drift by the kappa re-run, both kept on the board with their evidence rather than deleted (R-ANA-02).

effect.text: 8.6% of orders fail the customer's first look at the QC desk (135 of 1,566 in the 21-day baseline census, p-bar 0.086207 frozen and stable) -- the charter's baselined problem, tracked as the daily rejected proportion

causes.text: Jobs reach the cutter without a signed-off imposition -- fold and bleed get set per operator habit at prepress, so trim registration drifts from job to job
Proof approval closes the ticket in the operator's mind -- imposition gets set after approval, from memory, between other jobs

evidence.ref: Prepress walk with Jordan Pike (2026-07-27, six release-ready jobs): five of the six had imposition set after the customer proof was approved, from memory, with the traveler's imposition sign-off line blank -- the sign-off got circled only when someone remembered at the cutter.

causes.text: Prepress release has never had a written pre-flight step -- imposition, bleed, and stock checks live in individual habit, and a rushed morning skips them silently

evidence.ref: Traveler audit (2026-07-28, the COPQ's 40-traveler reprint sample re-pulled): 31 of the 40 rework loops started at prepress or trim with the imposition line unsigned, and each operator interviewed runs a different mental checklist -- nothing written exists for the release step. The chain's Improve-ready root: give release a written pre-flight (imposition, bleed, stock SKU against the ticket).

causes.text: Paper trays get reloaded between jobs with unlabeled stock, so the press pulls whatever sheet is in the tray when the SKU changes mid-shift
Smudge and banding marks cluster on rush jobs racked before full ink cure
Wrong-quantity orders trace to counting by lift thickness at the cutter instead of running the sheet counter on mixed-stock jobs
Humidity swings in the stock room curl the lighter paper stocks ahead of trim
Evening crew turns out a different defect mix than day crew -- if true, the causes would be people-shaped and the fix would split by shift
Reject calls drift between raters at the QC desk, moving the measured rate rather than the true one

evidence.ref: Two-rater kappa, re-run after the operational-definition fix (print-msa v2, 2026-06-27): kappa 0.8645, 96% agreement over the 50-order pre-study set -- Tessa's and Omar's calls are consistent, so drifting judgment does not explain the 8.6% level.
